purpose: Verify that an official or user-supplied document actually relates to the identified property, legal interest, event and date before extracting a property-specific fact.
source_basis: Tailte Éireann Land Registry copy and search services
Tailte Éireann Registry of Deeds search services

matching_rules.effect: If a current or historical folio number is available, match it exactly and record the source/date.
Compare the official property description with the target property; do not rely on a similar address alone.
Where a map or registry plan is relevant, compare the mapped parcel/reference and preserve the limits of what the map establishes.
Where an instrument is retrieved, establish that the instrument is associated with the relevant folio/dealing before extracting its contents as property-specific evidence.
Names and dates must correspond to the alleged transaction, succession event or other legal event.
The document/event date and registration date must be preserved separately; a document cannot be treated as a target-date register state merely because it predates that date.
Determine whether the property belongs in the Land Registry or Registry of Deeds evidence route for the relevant period.

extraction_rules: Only facts whose source document and property match are verified may enter the property-specific evidence layer.
A user-supplied deed can be relevant evidence but must not be treated as an official registration record merely because it appears authentic.
An official folio can establish registered facts within its scope; deeper legal conclusions may require the underlying instrument or other evidence.
A Registry of Deeds memorial/search result must not be treated as the text or legal effect of the underlying deed.
If multiple candidate properties match an address or party name, stop and request stronger property identification evidence rather than selecting one silently.
instrument_access_rule: Tailte Éireann states that completed dealings are registered on the folio and that the underlying title documents are filed in an Instrument; inspection of an Instrument is restricted to specified persons or routes under Rule 159.
guardrails: Never match a property solely by address.
Never treat a document's existence as proof of its legal effect.
Never treat an instrument as the current register without checking the folio/dealing outcome.
Never infer historical ownership from a current owner name without temporal evidence.
Never publish a property-specific fact until property identity and source identity are both verified.
